text:
Alice Morgan: Heads-up — I pushed the segment-compaction-adjust change to canary a few hours ago.
Ben Kim: saw that, thanks. Any perf numbers yet?
Alice Morgan: longctx perf tests started failing intermittently, a bunch of OOMs on the 64k+ sequence suite.
ci-bot: perf/longctx-suite: failed — OOM on worker-12 (job 4621). CI logs: https://ci.redwood/4621
Carla Soto: hmm, segment compaction shouldn't increase resident set like that. What's the heuristic tweak?
Alice Morgan: we lowered compaction aggression to avoid frequent small compactions; new algo merges nearby segments more eagerly into larger slabs.
Dmitri Volkov: merging into larger slabs would increase peak chunk size. Could interact badly with kernel-selection fastpath that assumes small slab locality.
Ben Kim: good call. Any cpu profiles or pmap dump from failing runs?
Alice Morgan: attaching relevant snippets from the failing host:

```
pss summary: kv-cache total RSS 9.8G
pmap -x kv_process | tail -n 10
  0x7f8c...  2,048K rw-s   [ anon ]
  0x7f8d...  3,072K rw-s   [ anon ]
  0x7f8e...  6,144K rw-s   [ anon ]
```

perf report shows heavy time in `kernel_router::select_kernels` after compaction.
Carla Soto: select_kernels hotpath scanning for segment boundaries? that should be O(segments) per request, strange.
Dmitri Volkov: if segments are fewer but bigger, KV-index lookup could cause more collisions and more linear scans inside slab metadata. That plus larger contiguous pages could trigger madvise/mmap fragmentation effects.
Elaine Ruiz: prod rollout is in progress, I paused the canary after seeing elevated OOM alerts and latency spikes. deploy-bot: rollout paused by Elaine R — reason: memory OOMs on canary.
deploy-bot: rollout status: PAUSED (canary stage) — action required.
Ben Kim: let's bisect between the compaction heuristic change and the previous kernel-router refactor from last week. Two suspects.
Alice Morgan: agree. I'll run a local bisect on the canary image set. Candidate commits: `a1f9c3` (seg-compact), `b7d2ff` (kernel-route-refactor).
Carla Soto: also repro locally with a synthetic longctx load? I can spin the longctx harness against the old vs new.
Dmitri Volkov: adding timing: with seg-compact enabled, avg kernel selection time jumps from 120us -> 430us for seq>32k.
Elaine Ruiz: note: we also saw increased GC churn in the runtime logs around compaction events.
Ben Kim: can you dump a heap profile around a compaction event? maybe we have a path that pins pages during merge.
Alice Morgan: will instrument. For now, rollback looks safest if we can't get a clean bisect within the hour. What's the rollback window for canary? deploy-bot: automatic rollback policy: 30m if major failure detected, manual override allowed.
Carla Soto: if we revert only the seg-compact commit, we can keep the kernel-router refactor. I'd prefer minimal blast radius.
Dmitri Volkov: agree — the kernel-router refactor had unit tests and perf baseline. The compaction heuristic is more experimental.
Elaine Ruiz: I'll prepare the rollback PR and hold the broader rollout until we confirm the root cause.
Alice Morgan: running instrumented build now with extra logging in the compaction code and kernel router. Will post profiles and flamegraphs shortly.
Ben Kim: once you have the profile, add a heatmap of seq-length vs RSS.
Alice Morgan: posted flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/2087654321
Alice Morgan: flamegraph shows compaction causing a 1.5s pause in `kv_cache::merge_segments` then a cascade into `select_kernels` where it spends majority scanning slab meta.
Carla Soto: interesting — the merge creates larger contiguous maps which then cause `madvise` heuristics to prefer different kernel paths. That would explain the selection delta.
Dmitri Volkov: hypothesis: slab merge increases page residency for KV hot prefixes, leading to more TLB pressure for longctx and more kernel selection fallbacks -> memory blowup under high concurrency.
Elaine Ruiz: ok proceeding with rollback of seg-compact in canary. I'll notify oncall and customers if needed.
Alice Morgan: thanks — will keep digging in parallel for a safer compaction algorithm (incremental merge + throttling).
Ben Kim: follow-up: add a canary test that runs the longctx suite under high concurrency for future compaction changes.
Elaine Ruiz: noted. I'll add a rollout gate for memory-sensitive heuristics.
Carla Soto: +1 on gate. Also consider exposing a runtime knob to disable eager merge without redeploy.
Alice Morgan: good idea, I'll add a feature flag.
Ben Kim: thanks everyone. Keep updates in this thread.
Elaine Ruiz: rollback initiated. deploy-bot: rollback started for canary image set (job 9812).
ci-bot: perf/longctx-suite: rerun queued (job 4622).
Alice Morgan: new run looks clean so far, no OOMs in first 30m.
Ben Kim: great. we'll reopen rollout after we have an incremental merge that avoids the kernel selection regression.
